(11 January 2025) | next_meeting = TBD | pushpin_map = Spain Asturias | pushpin_label1 = [[El Molinón]] | coordinates1 = {{coord|43|32|10|N|5|38|14|W|display=inline}} | pushpin_label2 = [[Estadio Carlos Tartiere|Carlos Tartiere]] | coordinates2 = {{coord|43.360783|-5.870222|display=inline}} | pushpin_caption = Location of the two teams' stadium }} The '''Asturian derby''' ({{langx|ast|Derbi asturianu}}, {{langx|es|Derbi asturiano}} or ''Derbi astur'') is the name given to any [[association football]] match contested between [[Sporting de Gijón]] and [[Real Oviedo]] (sometimes referred to as ''Carbayones''), the two biggest clubs in [[Asturias]]. The rivalry is well-known as one of the strongest, and most heated in [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. ==History== The first competitive match between the two teams happened on 5 December 1926, after the two main teams in Oviedo (Stadium Ovetense and Deportivo Oviedo) merged to create Real Oviedo. The match, in the [[Regional Championship of Asturias]], was played in [[El Molinón]] and Sporting Gijón won by 2–1.{{cite web|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1926/12/06/pagina-5/616682/pdf.html|publisher=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=6 December 1926|access-date=11 September 2017|title=R. Sporting 2-R. Oviedo 1}} The first official match in the Spanish league was played in February 1929, during the [[1929 Segunda División]]. Oviedo defeated Sporting by 6–2 with Barril scoring four goals in the second half. In 1944, the first derby in [[La Liga]] was played and the ''Carbayones'' won again 2–1. On 27 February 1966, just after the kickoff of the derby at El Molinón, several people were injured after an avalanche occurred in one of the stands of the stadium.{{cite web|url=http://hemeroteca.elcomercio.es/cgi-bin/Pandora.exe?fn=select;query=id:0000223561;xslt=pagina;publication=El%20Comercio;place=Gij%C3%B3n;day=01;month=03;year=1966;page=011;filename=66M01;encoding|title=Un "derby" limpio, correcto, que dio la victoria al Sporting por una diferencia tal vez raquítica|trans-title=A clean, correct "derby" that gave Sporting the victory for a perhaps rickety difference|publisher=[[El Comercio (Spain)|El Comercio]]|language=es|date=1 March 1966|access-date=27 February 2017}} On 29 May 1977 a special derby was held in Oviedo, where Sporting won by 2–1 at Estadio Carlos Tartiere in the penultimate match of the [[1976–77 Segunda División]], achieving promotion to [[La Liga]] and beginning the 'golden years' of the club.{{cite web|url=http://hemeroteca.elcomercio.es/cgi-bin/Pandora.exe?fn=select;query=id:0000112189;xslt=pagina;publication=El%20Comercio;place=Gij%C3%B3n;day=31;month=05;year=1977;page=030;filename=77Y31;encoding|publisher=El Comercio|language=es|date=31 May 1977|access-date=30 May 2017|title=¡Campeones!}} [[File:El Molinón Sporting-Oviedo 2017-18.jpg|thumb|Kick off of the derby played in Gijón in 2017.]] On 15 March 1998, Oviedo won 2–1 in the last derby in La Liga to date. After [[1997–98 La Liga|that season]], Sporting were relegated to Segunda División with the worst performance ever in the Spanish top league.{{cite web|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1998/03/16/pagina-29/1388760/pdf.html#&mode=fullScreen|title=El derbi, para el Oviedo|publisher=Mundo Deportivo|date=16 March 1998|language=es|access-date=3 March 2017}} This was also the last Asturian derby played at the old [[Estadio Carlos Tartiere (1932)|Estadio Carlos Tartiere]] before its closure in May 2000. The first derby at the new [[Estadio Carlos Tartiere]] was played on 28 October 2001, being the first ever sell-out for the venue; Sporting beat the locals 2–0. In 2003, the clubs played the last derby before the relegation of Oviedo to [[Segunda División B]], later dropped to [[Tercera División]] due to nonpayments. Oviedo won by 2–1. After Oviedo's second goal, one of the stands collapsed and several fans went onto the pitch, without any injuries. Due to this, Estadio Carlos Tartiere was closed for one game.{{cite web|url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD03/PUB/2003/05/19/EMD20030519035MDP.pdf|title=El Oviedo gana al Sporting y se aferra a la permanencia|trans-title=Oviedo beats Sporting and clings to permanence|publisher=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=19 May 2003|access-date=3 March 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2003/06/03/mas_futbol/1054591227_850215.html|title=El Carlos Tartiere, clausurado por un partido|trans-title=The Carlos Tartiere, closed for one match|publisher=[[Diario As]]|date=3 June 2003|language=es|access-date=3 March 2017}} After Oviedo were relegated to the lower divisions, the club had to play against [[Sporting de Gijón B|Sporting B]] for several years until their comeback to Segunda División in 2015. Oviedo and Sporting met again on 9 September 2017, in the fourth round of the [[2017–18 Segunda División]], breaking the biggest gap ever (14 years) without facing each other in official competitions. The match, played in Gijón, ended with a one-goal draw.{{cite web|url=http://www.lne.es/deportes/2017/09/10/buenos-hermanos/2161362.html|publisher=[[La Nueva España]]|date=10 September 2017|access-date=10 September 2017|title=Como buenos hermanos|trans-title=Like good brothers|language=es}} Before it, in the surroundings of the stadium, there were altercations between the [[National Police Corps|National Police]] and the [[ultras]] of Sporting Gijón, ending with damage to the buses of both clubs and 12 persons arrested.{{cite web |date=12 September 2017 |title=La Policía cierra la investigación de los ultras del Sporting con doce detenidos |trans-title=The police closed the investigation of the Sporting ultras with twelve detainees |url=http://www.elcomercio.es/gijon/detenidos-once-ultras-20170912000507-ntvo.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912192141/http://www.elcomercio.es/gijon/detenidos-once-ultras-20170912000507-ntvo.html |archive-date=2017-09-12 |access-date=12 September 2017 |publisher=El Comercio |language=es}} In the second-leg match played in [[Carlos Tartiere]], Oviedo defeated Sporting by 2–1. The second derby of the [[2019–20 Segunda División|2019–20 season]], initially dated for 29 March 2020, was postponed due to the [[2020 coronavirus pandemic in Asturias|coronavirus pandemic]]. It finally was played on 22 June at El Molinón, behind closed doors, and finished with the win of the ''carbayones'' by 0–1.{{cite web|url=https://www.elcomercio.es/deportes/futbol/oviedo-toma-aire-costa-sporting-20200622234520-nt.html|publisher=[[El Comercio (Spain)|El Comercio]]|date=23 June 2020|title=El Real Oviedo toma aire a costa del Sporting (0-1)|language=es}} ==The derby in the society== In April 2000, when both clubs were suffering acute financial trouble, there were rumours about meetings between the board of directors of both clubs to discuss a merger to create a single team in the region called ''Real Asturias'', and to study the possibility of building a new stadium between Oviedo and Gijón. Supporters of both clubs and the vast majority of the institutions were opposed to this proposal.{{cite web|url=http://masdeporte.as.com/masdeporte/2003/06/18/polideportivo/1055909797_850215.html|publisher=Diario As|date=19 June 2003|access-date=2 February 2017|language=es|title=La crisis reabre el debate sobre la fusión|trans-title=The crisis reopens the debate on fusion}} In 2017, the [[Non-governmental organisation]] ''Asturies por África'' (''Asturias for Africa'') organised an Asturian derby in [[Gambia]], played by local boys, to raise funds to build a new solar-powered well in the village of Ndungu Kebbeh.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/apr/07/real-oviedo-sporting-gijon-safe-water-gambia|title=A Spanish derby in the Gambia to bring joy and water to villages|work=The Guardian|date=7 April 2017|access-date=9 April 2017}} ==Head-to-head statistics== {|class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" |- !
